title: The Daumier fine
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The Daumier book has been overdue on the instructor's card since February. The library sends her a notice. She hands Wood the notice in the hall without stopping. He returns the book and pays the fine in dimes. The librarian counts them without comment.

panels.composition: A library notice, the letterhead as blocks, a date, an amount as a smudge, the INSTRUCTOR's name as blocks.

image.prompt: close on a printed library overdue notice with the amount smudged, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The hall. The instructor passing WOOD, the notice going from her hand to his without either stopping. The drop, again.

image.prompt: a woman instructor passing a young man in a college hallway and handing him a slip of paper without either stopping, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The library desk. The Daumier on it. Wood counting dimes from the cigar box onto the counter. The LIBRARIAN's cardigan.

image.prompt: a young man counting dimes onto a library desk beside a heavy returned book while a librarian in a cardigan waits, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The librarian's hand sweeping the dimes into a drawer. The book going onto a cart. Four months. Worth it. The strip says so with the book's spine, drawn as the panel's one solid thing.

image.prompt: close on a librarian's hand sweeping dimes into a drawer beside a heavy book on a cart, the book's spine dark and solid, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Four months on her card. Paid in dimes. 'I never did this,' twice over.
